title: project list
description: The projects added on this machine, from project list; project add and project remove answer it too, as it stands after the change. One server serves every project in it (ED-MISSION-2), so a reader such as the board's picker gets every project, and why one is unavailable, in one answer.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/designer/app/v1: the form of e-designer's answers. An app's answers keep the family app (apiversion/v1/forms.yaml), apart from the files they describe.

kind.description: Always ProjectList, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

ran.description: Where the answer came from; this contract fixes the app and the contract version, so an answer from anything else fails here.

app.description: Always designer, e-designer's product ID, since only e-designer gives this answer.

contract.description: Always v1, the contract version this schema belongs to.

data.description: One row per project, in the order they were added; empty when none is added.

items.description: One project: a folder holding a .designer/ design root. A project that cannot be read is still a row, saying why, so a reader lists every project and the rest carry on.

name.description: The project's name on this machine, unique in the list: the name --project takes and a picker shows. It is the folder's name unless another was given when it was added, so two folders with the same name can both be added.

path.description: The project's folder on this machine, absolute: the folder holding .designer/. The list is kept on the machine, never in a repository, so the path is only meaningful here.

designs.description: The ids of the designs in the project's .designer/, sorted, so a reader can offer them without asking again. Present exactly when the project reads.

items.description: A design's id, its folder's name.

unreadable.description: Why the project cannot be read, such as its folder being gone or holding no .designer/; present only then. Such a row names no designs, since an empty list would claim the project holds none, so a reader still lists the project and shows why it is unavailable.
